descriptor.implementation: string learned index (shared prefix + conditional reference)

memory.accounting_notes: index_owned_bytes is the sum of memory_breakdown()'s nine fields (block bytes, model tables, region prefixes, overflow containers, capacity tables, boundary directories, per-region objects, fences, index-level metadata); the fields are disjoint by construction, so the sum is not double-counted. adapter_owned_bytes covers only the adapter object and its query Mode. retained_input_bytes is 0 because the Row->Pair conversion buffer is released after bulk_load and the implementation holds its own copy. Returned rows from scan are owned by the caller and are not counted here.

descriptor.adaptation_notes: libart COPIES the key into its leaf (make_leaf memcpys it) but stores the VALUE as the pointer it is given, so this adapter owns only a stable array of values and no key copies at all. find() requires no conversion: libart takes (pointer, length) and the contract supplies exactly that, so there is no scratch buffer, no terminator and no per-query copy. update is adapted: libart has no update primitive, so this adapter searches and then writes through the returned pointer, which keeps update from inserting. scan is adapted and NOT seekable: libart iterates in order from the first key, so reaching lower_bound costs a walk over every key below it -- O(keys below the bound), not O(returned rows) -- and the walk stops as soon as the requested rows are collected.

memory.accounting_notes: index_owned_bytes is unavailable: libart has no allocation hook and no byte accounting, and estimating it from node counts would be an invention rather than a measurement. adapter_owned_bytes covers exactly one container -- the deque of values that libart's leaves point at, counted at its live size because a deque's element storage is not its capacity. There is no key arena: libart copies each key into its own leaf, so keeping one would be a redundant second copy of every key. retained_input_bytes is 0: the harness rows are passed straight to libart, which copies what it needs. Because the index's own bytes are unavailable here, THIS ADAPTER'S MEMORY FIGURE IS NOT COMPARABLE with an implementation that reports its own.

descriptor.adaptation_notes: HOT's value type must fit in a pointer (its interface static-asserts this), so the trie stores pointers to adapter-owned records and PairPointerKeyExtractor supplies the key. HOT's key type is a NUL-terminated const char*, so stored keys are copied into an arena that carries a terminator after each one and find() copies the queried key into a reusable scratch buffer to add one: one memcpy per lookup, no allocation after warm-up. That per-lookup copy is the cost of addressing by terminator and it is not zero. A key containing a NUL cannot be represented and is declared unsupported. update is adapted: HOT has no update primitive, so this adapter looks up first and then removes and re-inserts, which keeps update from inserting. scan uses HOT's native lower_bound, so its cost is the returned rows rather than the keys below the bound; the only adaptation there is a NUL-terminated copy of the bound, because the key type is a C string.

memory.accounting_notes: index_owned_bytes is unavailable: HOT reports node-type statistics but no byte accounting, and deriving bytes from node counts would be an estimate rather than a measurement. adapter_owned_bytes is exact and covers the NUL-terminated key arena and the record array -- the two things this adapter must own because HOT stores the pointers it is given and addresses keys by terminator. retained_input_bytes is 0: the harness rows are copied into the arena and not referenced afterwards. Because the index's own bytes are unavailable here, THIS ADAPTER'S MEMORY FIGURE IS NOT COMPARABLE with an implementation that reports its own.

descriptor.adaptation_notes: Single-threaded. Borrowed immutable bulk rows, stable owned insert rows. Exact unsigned-byte semantics. No neural network or hotspot cache. 32-bit record IDs limit total records to UINT32_MAX.

memory.accounting_notes: Capacity-based estimate; borrowed input counted in full. Excludes allocator headers, deque spare blocks/map, transient training/merge allocations. Not peak RSS; IDs/tags are owned, payloads of bulk rows are borrowed.
